Ripley's K function

Source: R/sp.R
ripk.Rd

Ripley's K function of a point pattern in the rectangle win at radii r, and Besag's L = sqrt(K / pi). Under complete spatial randomness K(r) = pi r^2 and L(r) = r. Four estimators: "none" (no edge correction), "border" (only points at least r from the edge are centres), "modif" (the modified border estimator, with the area of the eroded window; NaN once r reaches half a side) and "iso" (Ripley's isotropic correction, each pair weighted by the inverse of the share of the circle through the other point that lies in the rectangle, computed exactly). The normalisation is n (n - 1), as in spatstat.

Usage

ripk(x, y = NULL, win, r, corr = "iso")

Arguments

x, y

The points in planar coordinates (project longitude and latitude with eqproj() first): x and y numeric vectors of equal length, or x a matrix or data frame with columns named x and y (an unnamed two-column matrix is read as x then y). At least two points, all inside win; no missing values.

win

The study rectangle c(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax), in the unit of the coordinates. The intensity is the number of points over its area.

r

The radii: non-negative numbers in strictly increasing order, in the unit of the coordinates.

corr

The edge correction: "iso", "border", "modif" or "none".

Value

A data frame with one row per radius: r, k (in the square of the coordinates' unit) and l.

References

Ripley, B. D. (1976). The second-order analysis of stationary point processes. Journal of Applied Probability, 13(2), 255-266. doi:10.2307/3212829

Ripley, B. D. (1977). Modelling spatial patterns. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B, 39(2), 172-212. doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1977.tb01615.x

Examples

set.seed(1)
ripk(runif(100), runif(100), win = c(0, 1, 0, 1), r = seq(0, 0.25, 0.05))
#>      r           k          l
#> 1 0.00 0.000000000 0.00000000
#> 2 0.05 0.007686885 0.04946525
#> 3 0.10 0.033207387 0.10281167
#> 4 0.15 0.080766297 0.16033936
#> 5 0.20 0.131964756 0.20495289
#> 6 0.25 0.201545381 0.25328618
